content:
A 32-year-old mother in Mitchell, Indiana, has been arrested and charged after her 22-month-old daughter was found unresponsive in a bathtub and later died, according to Indiana State Police and court records.

Amanda B. Lane faces a felony charge of neglect of a dependent resulting in death in connection with the death of her daughter, Juliana Lucille Payton, authorities said.

According to a probable cause affidavit cited by local outlets, a witness who was helping at the home that morning placed the toddler in about one to two inches of warm water at Lane's request to help with a diaper rash, washed her, and left around 10:30 a.m. after confirming Lane knew the child was in the tub.

Phone records show the witness later checked in, and Lane allegedly replied around 11:24 a.m. that she could not get the child out and was upset, then said she had it handled, according to the affidavit.

The child's father returned home shortly before noon on Thursday, Nov. 5, after a court appearance and a stop for groceries, and asked where their daughter was. Lane said she was in the bathtub, and he found the toddler floating face down and unresponsive, according to the affidavit. He called 911.

Responders found the child with severe burns, and officers measured the bathwater at 118 degrees, according to reporting from FOX59. The child was taken to IU Health in Bedford, where she later died.

Lane was arrested without incident and booked into the Lawrence County Jail, Indiana State Police said. She appeared in court on Monday, Nov. 9. Prosecutors are seeking a habitual-offender sentencing enhancement, according to court records. Lane previously served more than two years in prison following a methamphetamine possession conviction and was released in 2023, according to Indiana prison records reviewed by PEOPLE.

The charges are allegations. Lane is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

Sources: Indiana State Police; FOX59; PEOPLE; WBIW; Lawrence County Independent

title: Indiana Mother Charged After Toddler Dies in 118-Degree Bathtub
